situation:
You are the product manager for OAK STREET SUB SHOPS, a sandwich and sub franchise with fourteen shops. The company has stayed in the same family for three generations, and a grandchild of the founder, the owner (judge), runs it now. The owner (judge) has asked you to recommend how the shops should run the make line through the lunch rush.

Sliced meats and prepped toppings sit in an open rail on the make line, and the brand's rules hold prepped toppings for four hours. Anything past that is thrown out. Crew members who are ill must report it and stay off the line, which on a heavy day leaves the rail short of hands as well as short of toppings.

Customers say the same two things in their reviews: the toppings look tired late in the day, and shops run out of them before the rush ends. Fresh food built in front of the customer is what the family has sold for sixty years. A delivery contract could bring a third more lunch business next year, but that number is a forecast, not a signed order.

Financing refrigerated rails for all fourteen shops would hold toppings safely through a full shift, but the payoff rests on the forecast of a third more lunch business, and if that volume never arrives the family carries a five-year loan its cash flow cannot cover. Prepping small batches twice through the rush instead costs nothing to buy but adds labor hours every day and still lets shops run out mid-rush.

The owner (judge) wants your recommendation on which way the shops should go, and on what it would take to put it in place. You will present in the back room of the shop. The owner (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the owner's questions, the owner (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the owner (judge) of OAK STREET SUB SHOPS, the third generation of the family to run it. Business background is the same as the situation above. You want the product manager to recommend whether the shops finance refrigerated rails or keep prepping small batches through the rush, and to walk you through what putting that recommendation in place would actually involve.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: What happens in the first week if we go with your recommendation?
Who has to be trained, and when?
